# Build manysearch CSVs
## Builds combined csvs from the manysearch run.


```{r setup}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
```

### Naming
`manysearch_gate3_recov1` means "any 3 saves all 1". A reference genome with ≥ 3 intersect hashes (`ih`) in any one metagenome is eligible for recovery. Every one of its hits is then kept down to 1 ih, in every metagenome.

### Rebuild rule
An output is rebuilt if it's missing, or if any `SRR*.csv` in `../manysearch/` is newer than it. Very snakemake inspired, very chic. A new SRR triggers a rebuild, and so does `touch ../manysearch/SRR*.csv`. Deleting an SRR does not, so touch the rest afterward.

## Parameters
`gate_ih_min`: Reference genomes that meet the `gate_ih_min` threshold in ANY one metagenome are eligible for recovery in every metagenome.

`recov_ih_min`: If a reference genome's hash intersection meets the `gate_ih_min` threshold in ANY one metagenome, its hits in other metagenomes are kept as long as they meet this threshold.


```{r params}
gate_ih_min  <- 3  # "any x": ref genomes with >= this many ih in ANY one metagenome are eligible for recovery
recov_ih_min <- 1  # "saves all y": hits from genomes eligible for recovery are kept at >= this many ih

in_dir <- "../manysearch"
tag    <- sprintf("gate%d_recov%d", gate_ih_min, recov_ih_min)

files <- list.files(in_dir, pattern = "^SRR.*\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
n_srr <- length(files)

# outputs
all_file <- file.path(in_dir, "manysearch_all_hits.csv")          # every raw row, every column
out_file <- file.path(in_dir, sprintf("manysearch_%s.csv", tag))  # any 3 saves all 1

# full read: lock key column types so every file reads identically
manysearch_types <- cols(
  query_name       = col_character(),
  match_name       = col_character(),
  intersect_hashes = col_double(),
  .default         = col_guess()
)

# slim read: only the 3 columns the analysis needs
read_ms <- function(f) {
  read_csv(f,
           col_select = c(query_name, match_name, intersect_hashes),
           col_types  = cols(query_name = "c", match_name = "c", intersect_hashes = "d"),
           show_col_types = FALSE)
}
```

## Do we need to rebuild?

```{r check}
# an output is stale if it's missing or any raw SRR csv is newer
stale <- \(f) !file.exists(f) || any(file.mtime(files) > file.mtime(f))

need_all   <- stale(all_file)
need_recov <- stale(out_file)

cat(n_srr, "SRR csvs in", in_dir, "\n")
cat("all hits:", if (need_all)   "REBUILD" else "up to date", "\n")
cat("recovery:", if (need_recov) "REBUILD" else "up to date", "\n")
```

## Pass 1: all hits + genomes eligible for recovery

Writes every raw row to the all-hits CSV (if needed). A reference genome is eligible for recovery if it has ≥ `gate_ih_min` ih in ANY one metagenome ("any 3").

```{r pass1}
if (need_all || need_recov) {
  if (need_all) {
    all_tmp <- paste0(all_file, ".tmp")
    if (file.exists(all_tmp)) file.remove(all_tmp)
  }

  seen <- vector("list", n_srr)

  for (i in seq_along(files)) {
    # full read only when writing all hits; slim read is faster
    d <- if (need_all) {
      read_csv(files[i], col_types = manysearch_types, show_col_types = FALSE)
    } else {
      read_ms(files[i])
    }

    if (need_all) write_csv(d, all_tmp, append = i > 1)   # header written once

    seen[[i]] <- d %>%
      filter(intersect_hashes >= gate_ih_min) %>%
      distinct(query_name)
  }

  # rename only once complete, so a crash never leaves a "finished" file
  if (need_all) {
    file.rename(all_tmp, all_file)
    cat("All hits saved to", all_file, "\n")
  }

  eligible <- unique(bind_rows(seen)$query_name)
  cat(length(eligible), "genomes eligible for recovery (>=", gate_ih_min, "ih in any metagenome)\n")
}
```

## Pass 2: recovery

Re-reads the raw files. Every hit from a genome eligible for recovery is kept down to `recov_ih_min`, and everything else is dropped.

```{r pass2}
if (need_recov) {
  recov_list <- vector("list", n_srr)

  for (i in seq_along(files)) {
    d <- read_ms(files[i]) %>%
      filter(query_name %in% eligible,
             intersect_hashes >= recov_ih_min)

    n_recov <- sum(d$intersect_hashes < gate_ih_min)   # hits below the gate, kept by recovery
    cat(sprintf("%s : %d rows kept, %d recovered (< %d ih)\n",
                tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(files[i])),
                nrow(d), n_recov, gate_ih_min))

    recov_list[[i]] <- d
  }

  recovered <- bind_rows(recov_list)

  # species = words 2-3 of the genome name; once per genome, then joined (fast)
  species_key <- tibble(query_name = eligible) %>%
    mutate(species = word(str_trim(query_name), 2, 3))
  recovered <- left_join(recovered, species_key, by = "query_name")

  # temp file + rename, so a crash never leaves a "finished" file
  out_tmp <- paste0(out_file, ".tmp")
  write_csv(recovered, out_tmp)
  file.rename(out_tmp, out_file)
  cat(format(nrow(recovered), big.mark = ","), "rows saved to", out_file, "\n")
}
```

## Output status

```{r status}
report <- \(f, rebuilt) {
  if (rebuilt) {
    cat(sprintf('"%s" was regenerated\n', normalizePath(f)))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf('"%s"\n was not regenerated at this time \n (last built %s)\n\n',
                normalizePath(f), format(file.mtime(f), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")))
  }
}

report(all_file, need_all)
report(out_file, need_recov)
```

## Cleanup

```{r cleanup}
if (need_all || need_recov) {
  suppressWarnings(rm(seen, recov_list, recovered, species_key, d)); gc()
}

rm(list = ls())
gc()

```
